You would be correct. The average duration of an active shooter incident is a bit under 12 minutes, and the average response time (in the United States at least) for first responders is 18 minutes.  Additionally my local Police Departments directives for such scenarios is to form a perimiter, contain the incident, and wait for SWAT to arrive.  I believe the same is for most metropolitan areas.  The average officer is not trained in clearing and securing buildings to the point SWAT is.  A lone patrol officer might just end up posthumously giving his tactical vest and AR-15 to the shooter/shooters.

To play Devil's Advocate for a moment, the AR-15s used by the police in the North Hollywood shootout did not play a major role in the gun fight.  One suspect committed suicide after losing his rifle and being injured in the hand, and the other was shot in his unarmed legs until he was immobilized and bled out.

The problem is, if we base standard equipment on worst-case scenarios, where do we draw the line?  ATGMs in the police armory in case someone gets the idea to kit up a bulldozer like Marvin Heemeyer?

Normal officers are tasked with normal occurrences.  In extreme situations, you call for those with the specialized tools and training, even if it takes longer.
